hints: Look at Dot's and Enzo's statements. Each one clears a single person, so for which suspects are both of them true?
Dot's statement is true unless Dot did it, and Enzo's is true unless Rosa did. So if Enzo or Quinn did it, both are true.
Then a third comes true as well: Quinn's if it was Enzo, Rosa's if it was Quinn. That is one too many, so test Dot and Rosa.

solution.key_idea: If Enzo or Quinn did it, three statements come true, so only Dot and Rosa are left to test, and Rosa gives exactly two.
steps: Dot's statement is true unless Dot did it, and Enzo's is true unless Rosa did it.
If Enzo did it, Dot's, Enzo's and Quinn's statements are true. That is three, so it was not Enzo.
If Quinn did it, Dot's, Rosa's and Enzo's statements are true. Three again, so it was not Quinn.
If Dot did it, only Enzo's statement is true. One is too few.
If Rosa did it, Dot's and Rosa's statements are true, and Enzo's and Quinn's are false. Exactly two, so Rosa borrowed the rake.
solution.epilogue: Rosa had borrowed the rake at dawn to pick berries for her festival muffins, meaning to hang it back before anyone noticed. She returned it at a quarter to ten, with a dozen muffins.
